male.name: The Havyaka coffee farmer
male.tagline: Havyaka smallholder on family coffee, areca and pepper land, wary of disease, wildlife and ESA maps.

dayInLife.text: Walks the estate checking coffee bushes and areca palms for pests, wilting and yellowing.
Pruning and shade-tree management fill the days.
Sprays pesticide and fungicide ahead of the rains.
Hired pickers and he strip ripe cherries by hand, then pulp them at a small wet-mill.
Parchment dries on raised beds, then sells via a curing works or trader in Chikkamagaluru town.

topics.label: Daily Life & Work
topics.headline: Disease, wildlife and prices squeeze a five-acre estate
points: Intercrops Arabica coffee, arecanut and pepper; even his small output feeds a national export chain whose prices he cannot influence.
Areca Yellow Leaf Disease has no known cure, so he leans harder on coffee and pepper instead.
Elephants make hired labourers reluctant to work at dawn or dusk, costing picking days at peak harvest.

stat.label: Areca Yellow Leaf Disease incidence in Sringeri, Koppa, Narasimharajapura and Kalasa taluks

topics.label: Family & Household
topics.headline: Parents next door, children's futures pointing away from the estate
points: Lives on the family estate; his elderly parents occupy an adjoining portion and still weigh in on land decisions.
His wife works the harvest, supervising hired women pickers and managing the drying yard, besides running the household.
Worries his son's salaried ambitions leave open who manages the estate, amid a wider bride shortage for farming sons.

topics.label: Education & Schooling
topics.headline: Son boards for coaching; daughter's bus fails in monsoon
points: He studied only up to PUC at a government college in Chikkamagaluru town and wants his children to go further.
His Class 12 son boards in town for coaching; his Class 9 daughter's bus is unreliable in monsoon.
Free Shakti bus travel eases fares for his daughter, but monsoon road closures can still cancel the service.

stat.label: Karnataka female dropout rate, Classes 9-10 (UDISE+), against about 8% nationally

topics.label: Health & Wellbeing
topics.headline: Monkey fever, elephants and distant hospitals
points: Kyasanur Forest Disease is the risk most specific to him; transmission peaks January to May during coffee picking.
Elephants and, less often, leopards use nearby corridors, so he and his wife think twice about dawn and dusk paths.
Routine care is a Mudigere health centre and private clinic; serious cases mean Chikkamagaluru town via ghat roads.

stat.label: KFD infections across Chikkamagaluru and Shivamogga, 2025 season; at least two deaths

topics.label: Community & Belief
topics.headline: Havyaka kin networks, the temple, and a quietly watched shrine dispute
points: Social life runs through Havyaka farming families across the Mudigere-Koppa-Sringeri belt, who speak Havigannada alongside Kannada.
Weddings and temple gatherings double as chances to compare notes on disease, labour rates and rain.
Over the Baba Budangiri shrine dispute, he says Hindu and Muslim neighbours get along day to day.

topics.label: Civic Life & Government
topics.headline: The Western Ghats ESA draft dominates his civic attention
points: The 27 July 2026 draft risks classifying canopy-covered coffee and areca plantations like his own as natural forest.
Karnataka's legislature unanimously rejected the draft on 22 September 2026, seeking a one-year extension for a physical survey.
He finds Forest Department elephant-damage compensation slow and undervalued relative to actual crop losses.

stat.label: identified as ESA across ten Karnataka districts in 27 July 2026 draft

topics.label: Worldview & Concerns
topics.headline: Neglect and misclassification by authorities who miss plantation reality
points: Blames the ESA satellite methodology for mistaking working estates for forest; wants a survey-number-by-survey-number assessment first.
Sees research as failing to deliver a cure for areca Yellow Leaf Disease while farmers carry debt against dying trees.
Proud of coffee heritage, yet anxious about succession and about erratic blossom rains no scheme insures against.

schoolPressures.label: Harvest labour
schoolPressures.detail: Economic pressure can pull girls into farm labour during coffee harvest, when every extra pair of hands matters.

schoolPressures.label: Monsoon roads
schoolPressures.detail: His daughter's bus becomes unreliable when hill roads wash out in the heavy monsoon months.

schoolPressures.label: Girls' mobility
schoolPressures.detail: Concern over girls' mobility and perceived sexual purity grows once they reach adolescence.

schoolPressures.label: Protest bandhs
schoolPressures.detail: Sringeri's ESA bandh shut shops, banks and schools for a day, a land-rights disruption to schooling.

female.name: The Kodava homestay manager
female.tagline: Kodava woman running a coffee estate and family homestay in an ancestral clan house.

dayInLife.text: Oversees breakfast and check-out for guests in two converted rooms of the ainmane.
Walks the coffee-and-pepper plot with her husband and the estate's hired workers.
Manages homestay bookings, meals and the guest experience herself.
Picking season: labour demand peaks, and she helps organise housing for migrant worker families.

topics.label: Daily Life & Work
topics.headline: Estate and homestay mornings, with labour as the daily worry
points: Hired workers, mostly migrants from north Karnataka, Odisha, Assam or Jharkhand, now make up the bulk of the workforce.
The homestay began after the 1990s coffee price crash; she now competes with larger resorts entering the district.
Legal minimum wage is roughly Rs 270 for an eight-hour day, though many workers are paid less for longer hours.

stat.label: Estimated registered homestays in Kodagu, plus over 2,000 unregistered ones

topics.label: Family & Household
topics.headline: Joint household where Kodava custom gives women unusual standing
points: Married into a patrilineal okka clan; the estate's jamma land stays registered to the clan, not divided.
Shares the ainmane with her husband, his parents and two children; her mother-in-law helps with childcare and cooking.
Consulted on homestay investment, schooling and increasingly estate matters, while husband and father-in-law handle field supervision and traders.

topics.label: Education & Schooling
topics.headline: Daughter boards in Madikeri; floods and hostel costs shape others' schooling
points: Her daughter has boarded in Madikeri town since Class 8; village options and landslide-prone commutes fell short.
Migrant labourers' children often cannot access local schools because instruction is in Kannada and home languages differ.
Free Shakti bus travel has made her children's trips cheaper; she is confident both will finish secondary school.

stat.label: schools closed over a year after August 2018 landslides destroyed access roads

topics.label: Health & Wellbeing
topics.headline: Madikeri hospital at home, Mysuru for anything serious
points: Routine care uses primary health centres feeding a single district hospital in Madikeri; serious cases go to Mysuru.
The Madikeri-Mysuru road was repeatedly landslide-damaged between 2018 and 2020, making emergencies harder.
Elephants are a persistent estate presence, so she is careful about who moves through dense areas at dawn and dusk.

topics.label: Community & Belief
topics.headline: Kodava clans, martial festivals and a language of their own
points: Kodava identity centres on over a thousand named okka clans, each historically tied to an ancestral ainmane house.
Kail Podh in early September and Puthari, the November-December rice harvest festival, structure her year.
At home she and her husband speak Kodava Takk, a traditionally unwritten language; the children mix in Kannada and English.

stat.label: named patrilineal okka clans in the Kodava community

topics.label: Civic Life & Government
topics.headline: No railway, slow flood rehabilitation, and an ESA draft
points: Kodagu has no railway; a 2012 survey found a Mysuru-Kushalnagar line not viable, and by mid-2026 no proposal existed.
She welcomed the legislature's September 2026 resolution rejecting the ESA draft and demanding a physical survey, not satellite mapping.
Kodava landholders enjoy an Arms Act licensing exemption, most recently extended to 2029.

stat.label: displaced families still awaiting rehabilitation housing seven years after the 2018 landslides

topics.label: Worldview & Concerns
topics.headline: Chronic official neglect of a district the state benefits from
points: Blames successive governments for broken railway promises; wants a real connectivity plan or an honest admission none is coming.
Blames satellite mapping for confusing coffee estates with forest; wants a parcel-by-parcel survey excluding settled agricultural land.
Proud of Kodava culture and the homestay economy, yet uneasy about exploitative labour arrangements her family depends on.

schoolPressures.label: Limited village school
schoolPressures.detail: The family judged village school options beyond middle school too limited for the higher secondary years.

schoolPressures.label: Landslide roads
schoolPressures.detail: The daily commute on Kodagu's landslide-prone roads was judged too unreliable to sustain.

schoolPressures.label: Hostel costs
schoolPressures.detail: Families in remoter estate hamlets say they cannot always afford to place a child in a hostel.

schoolPressures.label: Flood disruption
schoolPressures.detail: A single monsoon season can knock a rural Kodagu child's schooling off track for a year or more.
